newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan signs $1 billion credit facility.
newsitem.headline: Alcan signs $1 billion credit facility.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd said on Friday that it signed a US$1 billion global multicurrency credit facility with a syndicate of banks.

The credit agreement would replace certain existing facilities and would be available for use by Alcan and designated subsidiaries for general corporate purposes, including the back-up of its commercial paper program, the company said.
In 1995, Alcan had US$947 million of committed term credit lines with banks, of which US$895 million was available and unused at year end.

Alcan spokesman Charles Belbin said the new credit facility was more flexible because it was global multicurrency and for seven-year term term rather than the three-year term of the previous facility.
He said the new facility also carried lower commitment fees and borrowing costs.
"This announcement today doesn't signify anything in terms of Alcan's strategy or plans. It's simply good financial management," Belbin said.
Belbin said that as in 1996, Alcan expected that cash generated from operations would be more than sufficient to meet planned capital expenditures and dividends.
